payload: architecture + sourceRefs on one module-level work/node@2 index.yaml
completion: Review proof and current .starciwork validation only; never implementation, Sonar or UAT pass.
handoff: Downstream consumes accepted requirement/AC/flow IDs unchanged and architecture code/service/security scope by reference. Missing decisions block the affected handoff.

action.en: Research exact FE/BE revisions, manifests, entrypoints, DI, API handlers, data stores, jobs, deploy topology and tests. Follow inbound callers and outbound consumers; cite repository/path/symbol/revision and distinguish observed paths from proposed paths. Trace each network hop from caller symbol through URL/config resolution, proxy/ingress wiring, receiving handler and deployment owner; record synchronous, async and in-process edges separately. Names and comments are clues, not endpoint proof. Keep observed and desired routing separate and block contradictory boundary decisions.

Map accepted business flow and AC IDs to responsible services and authoritative data writers. Draw the logical request/response and asynchronous event sequence in ordered flow rows, including trust boundaries; never assume a class is an independently deployed service. Write ordered serviceCalls with caller/callee service IDs, caller/receiver source refs, operation, endpoint binding, credentials/trust boundary, data classification, timeout/retry and evidence status. Verify response path and downstream side effects. Unobserved deployment/runtime facts remain unknown.

Choose and justify the smallest design meeting hard constraints, comparing alternatives where material. Specify API request/response/errors, compatibility, transaction, lock scope, idempotency, event ordering, retry limits, timeout, compensation and read-back. Unknowns stay explicit. Evaluate Saga, CQRS, transactional outbox/inbox, idempotency, concurrency control and resilience patterns against actual invariants. Each pattern decision says adopt/preserve/reject/defer, why, simpler alternative, trade-off, scope and proof. Saga requires participant-local transactions, durable orchestration/choreography state, compensation/pivot/retry and failure recovery; an outbox alone is not Saga. CQRS requires explicit read/write models and consistency/read-your-writes policy; separate handler filenames do not prove CQRS and CQRS does not require event sourcing or separate databases.

Write codeImpacts with exact repository/path/symbol, observed/proposed identity, direct/transitive relation, change/preserve/review decision, reason, caller chain, tests and protected paths. Write serviceImpacts with deployable owner, inbound/outbound consumers, stores/events, compatibility, rollout/rollback and observability; explain unaffected boundaries. Map every selected pattern and service call back to exact source symbols, data/event schemas, deployment/config owners and protected paths. Do not route traffic to a different service merely because its repository contains a matching resolver.

Review each trust boundary: authentication, object/tenant authorization, validation, credential custody, sensitive logs, external provider/AI input, replay and resource abuse where relevant. Link threat, server-side control owner, code/service impact and positive/negative AC. Record residual risks and decision owner without claiming a security audit ran. Add a threat model per trust boundary: assets, entry points, attacker capability, exploit path, impact, prevention/detection, control owner and negative acceptance. Assess object/function/property authorization, tenant isolation, token issuer/audience/scope and forwarding, SSRF/redirect/DNS/egress, injection, webhook authenticity/replay, resource/AI cost abuse, sensitive transcripts/logs and dependency risks when applicable. Mark non-applicability with evidence; unresolved high-impact risks need a decision owner and block acceptance.

Produce implementation ceilings, protected paths, dependencies and required checks from actual repository scripts/CI. Lint, typecheck, tests/coverage, build and Sonar execute inside FE/BE implement; this op specifies them only. Bind rollout/migration/cleanup plans without executing them. Preserve business expected results unchanged. Design failure-injection tests for wrong service target, unauthorized forwarding, stale reads, duplicate/out-of-order messages, crash after commit before publish, compensation failure and retry exhaustion as applicable; implementations run them. Author canonical user journeys and journeyCoverage links to flow/AC IDs using the shared journey contract; preserve accepted journeys unchanged in architecture. Do not convert internal service hops into UI actions. Browser-free scope may use an empty array only when no UAT acceptance is assigned.

Validate the compact module architecture and current .starciwork graph. Canonical index.yaml must contain target ownership, call chain, contracts, data/transaction/concurrency/security design, plus concrete Saga and CQRS designs. Put observed facts in observations and sourceRefs; record missing runtime mechanisms in gaps rather than claiming they exist. Architecture completion does not complete implementation or UAT.
